source: Curated benchmark of major US heavy-shipbuilding / fabrication yards (no public GIS layer exists; see scripts/build_shipyards.py docstring)

sites.name: Kiewit Offshore Services
sites.coord_note: Facility-approximate (2440 Kiewit Rd, on Corpus Christi Bay).
sites.note: 400-acre deepwater fabrication yard; houses the largest onshore lifting device in the Western Hemisphere (12,500-ton rated capacity) — builds offshore platform hulls/topsides (Appomattox, Jack & St. Malo). The single most directly analogous US capability to floating-reactor module assembly.

sites.name: Gulf Island Fabrication — Houma Facility
sites.coord_note: Facility-approximate (east bank of the Houma Navigation Canal).
sites.note: 630-acre fabrication yard ~30 mi from the Gulf of Mexico via the navigation canal; 400'x160' floating drydock rated to 15,000 tons. Heavy lifts, TLP/platform module integration, hull construction.

sites.name: Ingalls Shipbuilding
sites.note: Largest private employer in Mississippi; new-construction shipyard for Navy destroyers (Arleigh Burke class) and amphibious ships.

sites.name: Newport News Shipbuilding
sites.note: Largest US shipyard by employment; sole builder of Navy aircraft carriers and co-builder of Virginia-class submarines. Nuclear-vessel construction experience directly relevant to reactor-module handling and radiological work practices.

sites.name: Bath Iron Works
sites.note: Arleigh Burke-class destroyer new construction on the Kennebec River.

sites.name: Electric Boat — Groton
sites.note: Submarine (Virginia-class, Columbia-class) new construction. Deep nuclear-vessel construction and shielding-fabrication experience.

sites.name: Electric Boat — Quonset Point
sites.note: Submarine hull-module fabrication yard — large steel modules built here and barged to Groton for final assembly, a supply-chain shape similar to what a barge-built floating reactor module would need.

sites.name: NASSCO (National Steel and Shipbuilding Company)
sites.note: Largest full-service shipyard on the US West Coast; Navy auxiliary/support ship and commercial tanker new construction.

sites.name: Austal USA
sites.note: Independence-class Littoral Combat Ship and Spearhead-class expeditionary fast transport new construction (aluminum hulls).

sites.name: Philly Shipyard
sites.coord_note: Facility-approximate (former Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, Delaware River waterfront).
sites.note: Commercial vessel new construction (product tankers, container/RoRo ships) on the former Philadelphia Naval Shipyard site — itself a brownfield-to-shipyard conversion.

sites.name: Fincantieri Marinette Marine
sites.note: Great Lakes shipyard; Constellation-class frigate new construction. The Great Lakes-Seaway system's principal large-vessel yard.

sites.name: Vigor Portland (Swan Island)
sites.note: Large-vessel repair, conversion, and heavy fabrication on the Willamette River; no major new-hull construction program.

sites.name: Vigor Seattle (Harbor Island)
sites.note: Ferry and vessel repair, heavy steel fabrication.

sites.name: Puget Sound Naval Shipyard
sites.note: Largest naval shipyard on the West Coast by employment; aircraft-carrier and submarine overhaul/refueling — deep nuclear-vessel maintenance experience, no new construction.

sites.name: Norfolk Naval Shipyard
sites.note: Oldest and largest US naval shipyard; carrier and submarine overhaul, no new construction.

sites.name: Portsmouth Naval Shipyard
sites.note: Submarine overhaul and refueling; no new construction.
